landing.heroTitle: Decide right when communications go wrong
landing.heroBody: VYUHA gives each commander a different, degraded view of one hidden battle. Messages arrive late, garbled or not at all, and some orders are fake. Trainees record what they decided, how sure they were and why. The instructor then reviews what each of them saw against what was true.

1.title: Build the scenario
1.body: The instructor picks the map, the units and the events that break communications.

2.title: Hidden ground truth
2.body: The server keeps the one real battle. Trainees never see it.

3.title: Break the comms
3.body: Each message is delayed, dropped, corrupted or faked.

4.title: Decide under doubt
4.body: The trainee acts with a confidence percentage and a reason.

5.title: Replay and learn
5.body: The After Action Review shows what you saw against what was true.

landing.instructorBody: Run the exercise live with a view of the real battle beside every trainee’s picture, add events as it unfolds, then export the After Action Review as PDF, CSV or JSON.
landing.traineeBody: Join with the 6-character code from your instructor, work from your own map and messages, and see afterwards how your judgement compares with the truth.

summary.title: Trainee summary
summary.help: Correct = share of scored decisions that were right. Brier = calibration score, lower is better. Latency = seconds from the relevant information arriving to the decision. Grading = Admiralty grading accuracy against the hidden truth. Challenged = spoofed orders received that they challenged with Authenticate, with the count in brackets. Drift = average position error of their picture.

rules.NO_DECISIONS: Recorded no decisions during the exercise.
rules.ACTED_ON_LOW_GRADE: Acted on a report they had graded as unreliable {{count}} time(s).
rules.ACTED_ON_GHOST: Engaged or reported a ghost contact (no real unit behind it) {{count}} time(s).
rules.ACTED_ON_SPOOF: Acted on an order that had not been authenticated and was spoofed, {{count}} time(s).
rules.ACTED_ON_FAILED_AUTH: Acted on an order after authentication had shown it to be fake, {{count}} time(s).
rules.NEVER_AUTHENTICATED: Received {{received}} spoofed order(s) and never used Authenticate.
rules.SPOOF_HANDLED_WELL: Received {{received}} spoofed order(s) and authenticated before acting.
rules.OVERCONFIDENT: Overconfident: stated {{confidence}}% confidence on average but was correct {{accuracy}}% of the time ({{decisions}} scored decisions).
rules.UNDERCONFIDENT: Underconfident: stated {{confidence}}% confidence on average but was correct {{accuracy}}% of the time ({{decisions}} scored decisions).
rules.WELL_CALIBRATED: Well calibrated: stated {{confidence}}% confidence and was correct {{accuracy}}% of the time ({{decisions}} scored decisions).
rules.SLOW_DECISIONS: Decisions took {{seconds}} s on average after the relevant information arrived.
rules.GRADING_POOR: Report grading was poor: {{accuracy}}% accuracy over {{grades}} grades against the hidden true reliability.
rules.GRADING_GOOD: Report grading was good: {{accuracy}}% accuracy over {{grades}} grades.
rules.NEVER_GRADED: Received {{contacts}} contact reports and never graded one.
rules.HIGH_DRIFT: The picture was far from reality: on average {{errorM}} m of position error and {{missed}} hostile unit(s) missed.
rules.NO_SWITCH_WHILE_JAMMED: Team {{team}} did not switch away from heavily jammed {{channel}} for {{seconds}} s.
rules.SLOW_SWITCH: Team {{team}} took {{seconds}} s to leave jammed {{channel}}.
rules.QUICK_SWITCH: Team {{team}} left jammed {{channel}} after only {{seconds}} s: a good use of the PACE plan.
rules.LOW_SA: Situation awareness was low: {{score}} out of 100 on average over {{probes}} freeze probe(s).
rules.GOOD_SA: Situation awareness was strong: {{score}} out of 100 on average over {{probes}} freeze probe(s).
rules.ACTED_ON_SPOOFED_UAV: Acted on spoofed UAV data: engaged or reported up {{count}} contact(s) placed by a UAV whose navigation was being spoofed.

silentRidge.title: Op Silent Ridge
silentRidge.description: A blue platoon holds the Indus valley approaches to Leh while a hostile force probes from the northern ridgelines. Ridge-masked VHF, reliance-adaptive jamming, a SATCOM cyber outage and spoofed HQ orders force the team to reconcile conflicting pictures and fall back on PACE alternatives.

himPrahari.title: Op Him Prahari
himPrahari.description: A platoon holds the Nubra side of a 5,300 m pass while Battalion HQ sits on the Leh side. The ridge blocks VHF line of sight almost everywhere, so the team lives on HF and SATCOM, and then a planned SATCOM outage, HF jamming, a whiteout and a compromised C2 node take those away one by one.

tharKavach.title: Op Thar Kavach
tharKavach.description: A platoon screens open desert where line of sight runs for kilometres and VHF reaches everyone, until the adversary jams it hard. The team must move down its PACE plan while its own UAV, its best eyes on the flats, has its navigation spoofed and quietly reports every contact 2.5 km from where it really is.
